land.text: the same Thuringian land, continued in Cliopatria's next row from 476

successors.note: Not a dissolution: the Thuringii page shows one kingdom through the 5th and early 6th centuries; the 475/476 cut is Cliopatria's. The two dossiers should be one colour (rule 2).

keyframe_review.note: 40,557 km2 for 469-475, bbox 9.18-12.30 E, 49.25-51.92 N (today's Thuringia, the same shape as the next Cliopatria row). The Thuringii page: 'The Thuringi established an empire in the late fifth century'; Jordanes puts them 'immediately north of the Alemanni and Suevi in about 470'; the medieval kingdom 'lay between the Harz in the north and the Thuringian forest in the south', with early forms that 'may have extended further south, to northern Bavaria, and further east, to the Rhine between Mainz and Xanten'. No area figure on the page, so the infobox comparison is impossible. The Wikipedia page Cliopatria links ('Thuringian states', opened) is about the eight German states of 1871-1920 and says nothing of the 5th century; the Thuringii page is the one used.

region.text: Thuringia, between the Harz and the Thuringian forest

ledger.note: 469: the Thuringian kingdom appears in Thuringia. 'The Thuringi established an empire in the late fifth century' and Jordanes places them 'immediately north of the Alemanni and Suevi in about 470'; the page gives no founding year, so 469 is Cliopatria's row start (confidence 1). Eugippius (460s-470s) reports raids near Passau and Linz.

region.text: the Thuringian land, passing unchanged to the Cliopatria row Kingdom of Thuringia

ledger.note: 475: Cliopatria's first Thuringian row ends and its Kingdom of Thuringia row begins on the same land in 476. The Thuringii page shows no break (Basina, wife of the Thuringian king Bisinus and later of Childeric I, is dated c. 463-477 on her own page). The dissolve is the Cliopatria seam, not an event; merge the two dossiers if one state is wanted.

certainty.note: A tribal kingdom between the Harz and the Thuringian forest; no frontier is recorded and the early forms may have reached the Rhine.

sources.title: Thuringii
sources.note: Identity, 'late fifth century' empire, Jordanes about 470, boundaries (Harz to Thuringian forest), Frankish conquest 531-532. No infobox area, no capital.

sources.title: Thuringian states
sources.note: Opened because Cliopatria links it: the page is about the eight German states of 1871-1920 (Free State of Thuringia 1 May 1920) and does not cover the 5th century.

sources.title: Basina of Thuringia
sources.note: Person page: Basina c. 463-477, wife of Bisinus and then of Childeric I; Thuringia 'on the Gaulish or western side of the river Rhine' per Gregory of Tours. No territory.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Thuringian states' 469-475 (one shape, 40,557 km2) is the early Thuringian kingdom; its Wikipedia field points to the wrong article (the 1871-1920 states). It and the next row (Kingdom of Thuringia, 476-533, Wikidata Q268562, wiki title 'Basina of Thuringia', a person page) are one kingdom on the Thuringii page; two dossiers are written because the owned list has two slugs, and the seam at 475/476 is Cliopatria's. Whoever reconciles rows should merge them under thuringian-states (the earlier slug). No capital is given by any page opened, so capitals is empty. The Thuringii page puts Childeric I's refuge with the Thuringi at about 481 (Gregory of Tours and Fredegar, 'the story may be distorted'): it moves no border. Gazetteer: nothing new needed ({'region':'Thuringia'} exists); the Cliopatria shape is used as is. Page budget: Thuringii, Thuringian states, Basina of Thuringia (three pages shared by the two Thuringian dossiers).
